beginner_glossary.Burn-in (test): Stress-testing chips at high temperature and voltage to make the weak ones fail in the factory rather than in the field. It screens out 'infant mortality' defects, so only reliable chips ship. Aehr makes the equipment that does this. The more expensive and mission-critical the chip (AI processors, power devices, photonics), the more valuable burn-in becomes.
beginner_glossary.Wafer-Level Burn-In (WLBI) / FOX platfor: Testing/burning-in ALL the chips on a whole silicon wafer AT ONCE, before they are cut apart and packaged — saving cost on high-value devices. Aehr's 'FOX' systems (FOX-XP, FOX-NP) plus its 'WaferPak' full-wafer contactors do this. Aehr says FOX-XP is the only production-proven full-wafer test+burn-in for high-power devices (silicon carbide, photonics, AI processors).
beginner_glossary.Package-Level Burn-In (PLBI) / Sonoma pl: Burning-in chips AFTER they're packaged — the current industry standard for many parts. Aehr's 'Sonoma' (and Tahoe/Echo) systems, gained via the Incal Technology acquisition, do ultra-high-power package-level burn-in — important for power-hungry AI processors.
beginner_glossary.WaferPak: Aehr's full-wafer contactor — the consumable interface that connects the test system to every chip on a wafer. These are a recurring, higher-margin 'consumable' revenue stream alongside the systems.
beginner_glossary.Book-to-bill ratio: Bookings (new orders) divided by billings (revenue) in a period. Above 1.0 means orders are coming in faster than revenue is recognized — a sign of future growth. Aehr's was OVER 3.5x in Q3 FY2026 (orders far exceeded revenue), the core bull signal.
beginner_glossary.Bookings: The dollar value of new orders received. Aehr booked $37.2M in Q3 FY2026 — far above the $10.3M of revenue that quarter — pointing to a future revenue ramp IF those orders convert.
beginner_glossary.Silicon carbide (SiC) power semiconducto: A type of high-efficiency power chip used heavily in electric vehicles. SiC was Aehr's historical core market; the EV slowdown caused a downturn that cut Aehr's revenue from FY2024–FY2026.
beginner_glossary.AI processor / custom AI ASIC: The chips that run AI — either GPUs or custom 'ASICs' designed by hyperscalers (e.g., Google's TPU, Amazon's Trainium). They are large, expensive, and must be reliable, which is driving new demand for Aehr's burn-in.
beginner_glossary.HBM (High-Bandwidth Memory): Stacked memory placed next to an AI processor. Burning-in AI processors WITH HBM at high power is a new, demanding application Aehr is targeting (HTOL modules).
beginner_glossary.HTOL (High-Temperature Operating Life): A reliability/qualification test that runs chips hot for a long time to prove they'll last. Aehr is developing HTOL burn-in modules for high-power AI processors.
beginner_glossary.Silicon photonics / optical I/O: Chips that move data with light instead of electricity — used for fast data-center optical interconnects in AI clusters. Aehr won silicon-photonics customers for wafer-level burn-in of these optical ICs, a new growth vector tied to AI networking.
beginner_glossary.Hyperscaler: A giant cloud/AI company (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta). Aehr's 'lead hyperscale customer' is buying its burn-in systems for custom AI ASIC processors.
beginner_glossary.Total Addressable Market (TAM): The total potential sales opportunity. Aehr argues its TAM is expanding as it moves from SiC into AI processors, photonics, and memory — each a large new burn-in opportunity.
beginner_glossary.GAAP vs Non-GAAP: GAAP = official accounting results. Non-GAAP strips out items like stock-based compensation and one-offs. Aehr's GAAP and non-GAAP can differ (e.g., FY2025 GAAP was a small loss while non-GAAP was a small profit).
beginner_glossary.Price-to-sales (P/S): Market value divided by revenue. Because Aehr is small and currently unprofitable, P/E doesn't work; investors look at P/S — and Aehr's is very high (~75x trailing), reflecting big growth expectations baked into the stock.

company_snapshot.what_it_is: Aehr Test Systems is a small-cap maker of semiconductor TEST and BURN-IN equipment. Its machines stress-test chips (at high temperature/voltage) to weed out unreliable ones before they ship. In the AI/semiconductor supply chain it would sit in the EQUIPMENT tier (a reliability/burn-in tool vendor). Historically its core market was silicon-carbide (SiC) power chips for electric vehicles; that market is in a downturn, and Aehr is pivoting hard toward burn-in for AI PROCESSORS (custom ASICs with HBM), SILICON PHOTONICS (optical I/O for data-center interconnects), and memory — all tied to the AI data-center build-out.
company_snapshot.manufacturing_footprint: Designs and builds its FOX (wafer-level) and Sonoma (package-level) burn-in systems and WaferPak/consumables; U.S.-based operations (Fremont, CA). The Sonoma package-level burn-in line came via the acquisition of Incal Technology.
end_markets: AI processors / custom AI ASICs (with HBM)
Silicon carbide (SiC) power semiconductors (EV — legacy core, in downturn)
Flash memory, gallium nitride (GaN), and other high-value devices

business_model.summary: Aehr sells capital equipment (burn-in/test SYSTEMS) plus recurring CONSUMABLES (WaferPak full-wafer contactors and related parts). A customer buys a FOX (wafer-level) or Sonoma (package-level) system, then keeps buying the consumables and additional capacity as production scales. The business is lumpy and customer-concentrated: a few large orders can swing a quarter. The thesis is a market shift — from a SiC/EV downturn that has been shrinking revenue, toward a much larger AI/data-center burn-in opportunity (AI processors, photonics, memory) where Aehr's high-power, wafer-level capability is differentiated. The leading indicator is BOOKINGS, which have inflected sharply even while reported revenue is still depressed.
how_they_make_money: Burn-in/test SYSTEMS: FOX wafer-level (WLBI) and Sonoma package-level (PLBI) systems sold to chipmakers, test houses, and hyperscalers. [company releases 2026]
CONSUMABLES & contactors: WaferPak full-wafer contactors and related recurring parts that scale with customers' production volumes — a stickier, higher-margin stream. [company releases]
Service/support and capacity add-ons: follow-on orders as customers expand burn-in capacity (a recurring pattern with the lead hyperscale and photonics customers). [company releases 2026]
competitive_moat_analyst_view: Differentiated high-power, wafer-level burn-in: Aehr positions FOX-XP as the only production-proven FULL-WAFER test+burn-in for high-power devices (SiC, photonics, AI processors) — a hard, specialized capability. [company releases]
Dual-platform reach: wafer-level (FOX) PLUS package-level (Sonoma) lets Aehr serve both pre- and post-package burn-in, widening its addressable market. [company releases]

Early AI-burn-in positioning + reference wins: initial Sonoma order from a lead hyperscaler's next-gen AI ASIC, a paid 300mm wafer-level evaluation with a top-tier AI processor supplier, and new silicon-photonics customers — reference accounts in fast-growing markets. [company releases 2026]
Consumables lock-in: once a customer standardizes on Aehr's WaferPak/system, ongoing consumable and capacity purchases follow.

ASSUMPTION-flavored: these are real edges, but Aehr is SMALL, customer-concentrated, and the AI-burn-in opportunity is still mostly in BOOKINGS/evaluations rather than proven, recurring high-volume revenue.

revenue_streams.analyst_view: Aehr's income statement and its order book are telling OPPOSITE stories right now: revenue is DOWN (SiC/EV trough — $10.3M in Q3) while BOOKINGS are inflecting UP (>$37M, book-to-bill 3.5x) on AI processors and silicon photonics. That divergence is the entire investment debate. The bulls focus on the bookings/TAM-expansion (AI burn-in as a multi-year driver replacing SiC); the bears note that revenue is still small and declining, the company is unprofitable, and the wins are early (evaluations, initial orders) rather than proven high-volume production. Until bookings convert into sustained revenue, the reported financials will look weak relative to the stock's expectations.

competitors.landscape_summary: Aehr is a niche specialist in wafer-level and high-power burn-in. It competes with larger, broader semiconductor test & burn-in equipment makers and with chipmakers' in-house/alternative test approaches. Its edge is specialized high-power, full-wafer burn-in; its disadvantage is small size and customer concentration versus much bigger test-equipment peers.

key_competitors.note: Japanese test-equipment giant (ATE/SoC test, incl. burn-in adjacencies) — far larger; a key AI-test beneficiary.
Major automated-test-equipment (ATE) maker; broad semiconductor test exposure including AI/HPC.
Test handling, interface, and inspection; competes/overlaps in back-end test and burn-in-adjacent equipment.
Large chipmakers and test houses may use internal or alternative burn-in methods rather than buying Aehr systems.
Specialty suppliers compete on the consumable (contactor/WaferPak-equivalent) layer.

competitors.differentiation_analyst_view: Aehr's differentiation is being a focused leader in HIGH-POWER, WAFER-LEVEL burn-in — a hard, specialized niche that matters for SiC, photonics, and high-power AI processors — plus a package-level option (Sonoma) for the standard flow. The risks are that (1) it is tiny relative to Advantest/Teradyne, (2) revenue is concentrated in a few large customers/orders, and (3) bigger players or customers' in-house solutions could encroach as AI burn-in becomes a larger prize. The competitive question is whether Aehr's early reference wins translate into a durable, scaling franchise before larger rivals fully target the same applications.

financial_performance.analyst_view: Aehr's financials show a company at a TROUGH in revenue (SiC/EV downturn) and currently unprofitable, but with a sharply inflecting ORDER book pointed at AI/data-center burn-in. FY2025 revenue was $59.0M (small GAAP loss), TTM revenue has fallen to ~$45M with an ~$11M net loss, yet Q3 FY2026 bookings of $37.2M (book-to-bill 3.5x) and H2 bookings guided to $60–80M imply a coming revenue ramp. The crux: this is a 'bookings-ahead-of-revenue' inflection story — credible given the named hyperscaler/photonics wins, but unproven until those orders show up as sustained, profitable revenue.

It should be judged on bookings conversion, TAM capture, and the path to profitability — not on today's revenue or earnings.

valuation.analyst_view: This is the report's most important honest flag: AEHR trades at ~$108 while the (sparse, April-dated) analyst targets cluster around $56–$68 — i.e., the stock is ~40% ABOVE consensus, on ~75x DECLINING sales, while unprofitable. That combination says the share price is driven by momentum and AI-burn-in optionality running ahead of both current fundamentals and analyst marks. The bull case (real, named hyperscaler/photonics wins; book-to-bill 3.5x; expanding TAM) is genuine, but the valuation prices in a lot of future success; the bear case is simply that a tiny, unprofitable, revenue-declining company at 75x sales has significant downside if the AI-burn-in ramp disappoints or is slower/lumpier than hoped. High risk, high volatility, binary-feeling on execution.

final_research_summary.one_paragraph: Aehr Test Systems (AEHR) is a small-cap maker of semiconductor BURN-IN and test equipment — machines that stress-test chips to screen out unreliable ones before they ship. (NOTE: it is not yet a node in this project's supply-chain graph; this is a standalone report.) Historically its core market was silicon-carbide (SiC) power chips for EVs; that market is in a downturn, so revenue has been FALLING — FY2025 (ended 2025-05-30) revenue was $59.0M (a small GAAP loss), and TTM revenue is ~$45.3M with an ~$11.4M net loss. The story is a PIVOT to AI: burn-in for AI processors (custom ASICs with HBM), silicon photonics (optical I/O for data-center interconnects), and memory. The evidence of that pivot is in the ORDER BOOK, not yet the income statement: Q3 FY2026 (ended 2026-02-27) revenue was just $10.3M, but BOOKINGS were $37.2M — a book-to-bill of over 3.5x — driven by an initial Sonoma order from a lead hyperscaler's next-gen AI ASIC, a paid 300mm wafer-level burn-in evaluation with a top-tier AI processor supplier, and new silicon-photonics wins; management guided H2 FY2026 bookings to the high end of $60–80M. The valuation is the central caution: at ~$108 the stock is up roughly 10x off its 52-week low ($10.89–$121.80 range) for a ~$3.41B market cap on ~$45M of DECLINING revenue (~75x trailing sales) while UNPROFITABLE — and it trades ~40% ABOVE the (thin, April-dated) analyst targets of ~$56–$68. What is FACT is a genuine, named AI/data-center burn-in bookings inflection (book-to-bill 3.5x) on top of a depressed, currently loss-making base; what is being PRICED is that those bookings convert into a much larger, profitable AI-burn-in franchise. The debate is execution/conversion and an extreme valuation, not whether the AI-burn-in opportunity is real.
